## 1. Executive assessment

[method] This is the expanded prelaunch State of AI Data Labs and Human Feedback, prepared by ScienceToStartup and published under the identity of Musa Ozdem. It is an evidence-linked analyst synthesis for buyers, research teams and contributors. It is not a published weekly edition. The report ledger contains no published predecessor, DOI or completed archive. The separately versioned evidence graph leaves canonical dataset 2.5.0 and its historical dates unchanged. The purpose is to make decisions inspectable: what a source actually documents, what the analyst concludes from it, what remains unknown and what evidence would change the conclusion.

[method] The pinned synthesis input contains 1,713 approved assertions, 65 qualifying suppliers, 152 distinct reviewed paper works, 63 dataset families and 21 benchmark families, computed with coverage method 1.3.0. All 39 legacy organizations have completed bounded inclusion audits; 38 have conclusive commercial dispositions, while BenchFlow remains commercially pending. The graph also preserves 26 quarantined candidate assertions and 39 historical assertions. These counts describe selected-source coverage. The eligible inventory remains a lower bound, the core is unfrozen, and the formal reference and screening launch audits are unfinished. Individual count floors do not establish completeness or publication readiness.

[analysis] The market is more intelligible when the comparison begins with the unit being bought. A participant platform, a managed annotation program, a licensed dataset, an evaluation service and an executable RL environment leave different responsibilities with the buyer. Prolific distinguishes participant access from managed collection; Snorkel describes refreshed non-exclusive products; Mercor describes expert task construction; Surge describes environments and verifiers. The analytical implication is to compare statements of work and accepted deliverables before comparing brand claims. This evidence supports a responsibility map within this sample, rather than a universal competitive ranking.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed), [candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series), [candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction), [candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments)

[analysis] The word human conceals several different supervision arrangements. Human-written source material, human task design, independently collected judgments, correction of model drafts and human review of a model-selected subset are not interchangeable inputs. HelpSteer3, UltraFeedback, FineWeb-Edu and the described DeepSeek-R1 cold-start process demonstrate distinct combinations. A buyer should ask where a person intervenes and what that person can observe. Nothing in this sample establishes that one provenance class always produces better models; the defensible comparison is whether the supervision target and validation design fit the intended task.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels), [next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback), [candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels), [cohort5.claim.deepseekr1.human-coldstart](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekr1.human-coldstart)

[analysis] Quality requires denominators and a theory of disagreement. HelpSteer3’s retained consensus, HelpSteer2’s closest-rating aggregation, InstructGPT’s ranked sets and DICES’ repeated safety judgments arise from different observation processes. A pair count can expand from rankings without adding independent people; a post-filter agreement result can improve while excluding difficult items; a majority can erase a meaningful minority. Procurement should preserve raw labels, exclusions and adjudication reasons. These are methodological judgments based on the documented workflows, not measured differences in supplier performance.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus), [next.claim.helpsteer2.qa](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.helpsteer2.qa), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets), [cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference)

[analysis] Executable outcomes improve observability but do not eliminate judgment. SWE-bench tests, OSWorld state checks, τ-bench database rewards and PaperBench rubric leaves expose concrete success conditions. Their papers also identify incomplete test coverage, damaging side effects, missed policy violations or judge limitations. A reliable acceptance plan therefore needs both outcome checks and a separate review of constraints, side effects and ambiguous failures. The evidence does not justify treating a passed verifier as a certification of deployment readiness or general professional competence.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring), [cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap), [cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit), [cohort6.claim.paperbench.judge-validation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.paperbench.judge-validation)

[analysis] Public financial and workforce numbers answer different questions. Appen’s annual group revenue, Proximal’s annualized pace, Scale’s cumulative contributor payout and Prolific’s active-participant disclosure do not form a common revenue, capacity or labor denominator. Labelbox financing combines equity and a credit facility. The report therefore offers a commercial evidence ledger and project-cost methodology rather than market-share estimates or a valuation league table. Missing disclosure remains unknown, and a large advertised pool does not establish current paid availability for a particular language, credential or task.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025), [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure), [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout), [candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool), [candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing)

[analysis] Rights, privacy and security must follow the exact material and service boundary. Marketplace terms, a website privacy notice, a training-data license, a worker agreement and a security attestation can cover different subjects. Defined.ai separates marketplace datasets from new collection; AfterQuery excludes customer processor work from its website policy; Mercor directs work-platform users to a separate notice; MathVista retains underlying image and question rights while restricting training use. The analyst judgment is to obtain project-specific evidence for each boundary. Public documentation completeness is useful for diligence, but it is not itself a quality or compliance rating.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation), [candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary), [candidate.supplier.mercor.privacy-scope](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.privacy-scope), [cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms)

[method] All nine executive finding identifiers from the previous unpublished synthesis are retained. The additional studies refine their evidence and limits: post-selection agreement differs from raw agreement; model-simulated feedback differs from live expert assistance; disclosure audits describe reporting; and observed costs depend on the counted work and time. These refinements do not create a published weekly comparison or rewrite a historical archive. Confidence remains attached to each scoped judgment and to the evidence that could change it.

[analysis] The added annotation studies strengthen a practical distinction between an improved retained dataset and an improved production process. HelpSteer2 raises agreement after selecting and filtering labels; the surgical-annotation study compares instruction conditions and subsequent QA; LabelAId measures a particular intervention against researcher-adjudicated labels. Those designs answer different questions. A buyer should require raw-input, excluded-item and final-acceptance denominators, plus independent error inspection, before interpreting a high agreement score or a QA stage as evidence of better delivered work.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection), [cohort9.claim.qualityassured.qa-result](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.qualityassured.qa-result), [cohort9.claim.qualityassured.limits-identity](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.qualityassured.limits-identity), [cohort9.claim.labelaid.adjudication-study](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.labelaid.adjudication-study), [cohort9.claim.labelaid.precision-time](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.labelaid.precision-time)

<a id="finding-delivery-unit-before-provider"></a>
### Analytical judgment: delivery-unit-before-provider

In this reviewed sample, a useful supplier comparison begins with the delivery unit: participant access, licensed data, custom tasks or executable environments\.

Buyer implication: Specify who owns task design, annotation, QA, rights clearance and acceptance before comparing proposals\.

Limitations: First-party offering descriptions do not establish interchangeable services, capacity, realized quality or a market-wide supplier ranking\.

Confidence: Moderate for this sample’s disclosed distinctions; low for prevalence outside it\.

Reasoning: Prolific distinguishes participant access and managed collection; Snorkel describes refreshed non-exclusive products; Mercor describes custom task construction; Surge offers environments and verifiers\. Their responsibilities differ even where capability labels overlap\. The expanded corpus also distinguishes engineering teams, managed evaluation, hosted compute and contract-limited talent acquisition; the comparison remains task-specific\.

What would change this assessment: Matched statements of work and independently checked deliveries could show that particular offerings meet the same requirement and permit narrower outcome comparisons\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed), [candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series), [candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.task-construction), [candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.surge_ai.rl-environments), [candidate.cohort4.g2i.contracting-scope-limit](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.g2i.contracting-scope-limit), [candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation)

<a id="finding-human-and-model-provenance"></a>
### Analytical judgment: human-and-model-provenance

Human content, human labels and human oversight are distinct provenance claims; the selected datasets contain materially different combinations\.

Buyer implication: Require a stage-level provenance manifest and test the label target relevant to the intended task\.

Limitations: The reviewed methods are source-reported and version-specific\. No universal advantage of human or synthetic labels is established\.

Confidence: High for the documented provenance distinctions; unestablished for comparative training outcomes\.

Reasoning: HelpSteer3 describes independent human preference annotations, UltraFeedback describes GPT-4 labels and FineWeb-Edu describes model-scored educational filtering\. Calling these one annotation category would erase the origin of the supervision signal\. The expanded methods also include human correction of model responses and model-generated process signals, reinforcing stage-level provenance\.

What would change this assessment: Independent task-matched validation with raw annotations and generation logs could support outcome comparisons or expose errors in the reported provenance\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.independent-human-labels), [next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.ultrafeedback.model_feedback), [candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.fineweb.synthetic-educational-labels), [cohort5.claim.deepseekv3.human-check](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekv3.human-check), [cohort8.claim.prime.online-prm](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.prime.online-prm), [cohort9.claim.recodeh.simulated-feedback](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.recodeh.simulated-feedback), [cohort9.claim.recodeh.metric-scope](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.recodeh.metric-scope), [cohort9.claim.ultrafeedback.simultaneous-rubrics](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.ultrafeedback.simultaneous-rubrics), [cohort9.claim.ultrafeedback.human-agreement](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.ultrafeedback.human-agreement)

<a id="finding-agreement-needs-denominators"></a>
### Analytical judgment: agreement-needs-denominators

Released agreement and preference-pair totals cannot be interpreted without the independent-judgment and exclusion denominators\.

Buyer implication: Request raw-to-retained counts, invalid-item rules, repeat labels, disagreement slices and corrected acceptance\.

Limitations: The reviewed workflows differ in task and sampling\. They cannot rank provider quality, and no common reliability measurement was executed\.

Confidence: High for the methodological distinction; low for transferring a numerical agreement result between workflows\.

Reasoning: HelpSteer3’s retained consensus, HelpSteer2’s post-filter closest-rating aggregation, InstructGPT’s ranked sets and DICES’ repeated judgments have different observation and selection denominators\. The added HelpSteer2 paper makes the exclusions explicit; the inference study limits normalized scores to within-pair comparisons; Gilardi excludes trained-rater disagreement from the accuracy reference\. These distinctions make raw counts, exclusions and adjudication necessary before comparison\.

What would change this assessment: A common held-out task with independent raw judgments and the same exclusion rules could make reliability comparisons meaningful\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.postfilter-consensus), [next.claim.helpsteer2.qa](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.helpsteer2.qa), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.single-contractor-comparisons](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.single-contractor-comparisons), [cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dices.expert-crowd-difference), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority), [cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection), [cohort9.claim.inherent.normalization-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.inherent.normalization-limit), [cohort9.claim.gilardi.gold-denominator](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.gilardi.gold-denominator)

<a id="finding-artifact-role-is-narrow"></a>
### Analytical judgment: artifact-role-is-narrow

Named artifact attribution is strongest when it preserves the exact contribution stage and release rather than extending a brand association across a family\.

Buyer implication: Ask for source-supported roles for the specific delivered artifact; keep recruitment, annotation, validation and authorship separate\.

Limitations: These examples do not reveal contract values, contribution shares, exhaustive supplier lists or causal provider performance\.

Confidence: High for the explicit scoped roles in this sample; incomplete for the broader supplier graph\.

Reasoning: HelpSteer3 names Scale and Translated for different subsets; the Prolific case establishes recruitment through a researcher-owned interface; U-MATH credits Toloka AI and Gradarius with validation of professor-authored problems\. These relationships support narrower claims than sole production\.

What would change this assessment: Additional artifact-specific acknowledgments, contributor records or contracts could establish further stages or revise the scope\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.helpsteer3-contribution), [next.claim.helpsteer3.translated](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.helpsteer3.translated), [candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.cohere-recruitment), [candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.umath-validation)

<a id="finding-benchmark-protocol-before-score"></a>
### Analytical judgment: benchmark-protocol-before-score

Benchmark family names alone are insufficient for comparing scores or deciding deployment readiness\.

Buyer implication: Freeze task version, candidate responses, aggregation and execution environment, then inspect errors on the buyer’s actual task\.

Limitations: No benchmark was executed for this report\. The reviewed sources do not establish a universal deployment-quality ranking\.

Confidence: High for protocol differences and stated limitations; unestablished for any new system’s performance\.

Reasoning: RewardBench versions change scoring structure; TruthfulQA changes answer protocol and separates generation metrics; SWE-bench warns that passing tests does not ensure complete, efficient or readable solutions\. The measures answer different questions\. OSWorld and τ-bench additionally identify outcome-checking gaps for damaging side effects and policy violations\.

What would change this assessment: Reproducible matched-protocol results and independently checked target-task outcomes could support a narrower comparative claim\.

Approved evidence: [next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.rewardbench.v1.scoring), [next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.rewardbench.v2.scoring), [next.claim.truthfulqa.metrics](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.truthfulqa.metrics), [next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.truthfulqa.binary_revision), [candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring), [cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap), [cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit)

<a id="finding-commercial-denominators-stay-separate"></a>
### Analytical judgment: commercial-denominators-stay-separate

The selected commercial disclosures cannot be combined into supplier market shares, production-capacity rankings or a common unit-cost comparison\.

Buyer implication: Retain period, currency, organizational scope, active-window definition and acceptance basis; obtain a project-specific quote and availability check\.

Limitations: Coverage is selected and incomplete\. Missing disclosure is unknown, not zero; the observed figures are not matched measures\.

Confidence: High for the incompatibility of these disclosed denominators; no confidence claim is made about market-wide shares\.

Reasoning: Appen reports full-year consolidated and geographic-segment revenue, Scale reports cumulative contributor payouts with unspecified period and dollar currency, and Prolific distinguishes active participants from a waitlist without defining the active window\. None supplies a matched current paid-work or human-data revenue denominator across suppliers\. Proximal’s annualized disclosure and Labelbox’s mixed financing add further incompatible commercial measures\.

What would change this assessment: Comparable segment accounts, audited activity windows and accepted-unit cost records across the same scope could permit limited financial or operational comparisons\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025), [candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025), [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout), [candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.active-pool), [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure), [candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing), [cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary), [cohort9.claim.earnings.work-unit-wages](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.earnings.work-unit-wages), [cohort9.claim.earnings.causality-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.earnings.causality-limit)

<a id="finding-multilingual-intersections-before-language-counts"></a>
### Analytical judgment: multilingual-intersections-before-language-counts

Multilingual suitability depends on language-domain-task intersections and native validity, rather than a language count alone\.

Buyer implication: Specify every required intersection, preserve translation/review provenance and calibrate the judge in the target locale\.

Limitations: These selected studies do not establish universal translation inferiority, global language coverage or a provider ranking\.

Confidence: Moderate for these documented methodological distinctions; unmeasured for current supplier performance\.

Reasoning: HelpSteer3 records missing intersections, M-IFEval changes language-inappropriate constraints, BenchMAX post-edits translations and MENLO measures localized dimensions\.

What would change this assessment: Matched native-authored, translated and post-edited task studies with independent target-locale evaluation could narrow or revise the judgment\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.missing-domain-intersections](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.helpsteer3.missing-domain-intersections), [cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.mifeval.japanese-filter), [cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.benchmax.pipeline), [cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.menlo.dimensions), [cohort9.claim.aya.dataset-composition](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.aya.dataset-composition), [cohort9.claim.aya.quality-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.aya.quality-limit), [cohort9.claim.helpsteer.language-cultural-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.helpsteer.language-cultural-limit)

<a id="finding-rights-follow-exact-material-and-service"></a>
### Analytical judgment: rights-follow-exact-material-and-service

Rights, privacy and security diligence must follow exact components, services and uses rather than a top-level policy or license label\.

Buyer implication: Obtain component rights and the actual project processing/security scope before accepting data or environments\.

Limitations: This is public-source evidence and methodological judgment, not legal advice, rights clearance or an assurance audit\.

Confidence: High for the documented scope differences; unestablished for legal compliance of particular deployments\.

Reasoning: AlpacaEval separates code/data terms, RewardBench retains component obligations, MathVista restricts training use and provider notices distinguish website from customer processing\.

What would change this assessment: Project-specific agreements, rights-holder permissions and independent scoped assurance evidence could resolve particular unknowns\.

Approved evidence: [cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license), [next.claim.rewardbench.terms](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.rewardbench.terms), [cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms), [candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.afterquery.processor-privacy-boundary), [cohort9.claim.wildchat.consent-gate](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.wildchat.consent-gate), [cohort9.claim.wildchat.anonymization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.wildchat.anonymization)

<a id="finding-verifiable-outcomes-need-side-effect-review"></a>
### Analytical judgment: verifiable-outcomes-need-side-effect-review

Executable success checks should be paired with independent review of constraints, side effects and verifier error\.

Buyer implication: Test valid alternatives, plausible shortcuts, harmful extra actions and infrastructure failures in the acceptance pilot\.

Limitations: No environment or provider was independently executed for this report, and no failure-prevalence estimate is claimed\.

Confidence: High for the stated benchmark limitations; unmeasured for any new buyer deployment\.

Reasoning: SWE-bench passing tests do not guarantee a complete solution; OSWorld identifies damaging-side-effect gaps; τ-bench notes missed policy violations; MBPP documents assertion gaming\.

What would change this assessment: A matched evaluation showing that the project verifier reliably detects the buyer’s critical constraints could narrow the need for additional manual review in that scope\.

Approved evidence: [candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring), [cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.osworld.side-effect-gap), [cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.taubench.reward-limit), [cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit)

## 2. Weekly developments and edition discipline

[method] Edition status as of 10 November 2026: prelaunch; archive not_published; DOI null; editions empty. Daily preparation targets 16:00 America/Los_Angeles. The planned weekly release check is Monday 09:00 after a Friday 17:00 captured-source cutoff. The next planned cutoff is Friday 13 November 2026 at 17:00 Pacific, represented as 2026-11-13T17:00:00-08:00, and the next planned weekly edition is Monday 16 November. A graph prepared on 10 November cannot demonstrate that this future cutoff has passed or that all later inputs are within it. These dates are a schedule, not a publication receipt.

[method] The weekly change unit is a versioned source-supported claim, not an increase in word count or an older paper newly encountered by the research team. Source publication date, described event date, capture timestamp, assertion as-of date, review timestamp and edition publication date remain separate. A capture performed on 9 November in Los Angeles may be dated 10 November UTC. It does not retroactively satisfy a 6 November cutoff. Later independent review can approve the captured content without changing the time at which the document was captured.

[method] This preparation extends the prior unpublished 1,446-assertion, 132-work synthesis to a pinned input of 1,713 approved assertions and 152 reviewed works. Twenty newly reviewed works add annotation, disagreement, multilingual, worker-time, documentation and interactive-feedback evidence. Twenty-six citation repairs replace quarantined source bindings with fresh approved IDs while preserving scientific values and qualifications. The increase describes research inputs and repairs, not events that all occurred this week, market growth, production capacity or an accuracy score. The planned future cutoff remains separate from this preparation date.

[sourced_fact] The commercial event dates illustrate why review time must not become news time. Labelbox’s financing announcement is dated 14 October 2026; Proximal’s annualized-revenue announcement is dated 29 September 2026; Mercor’s 25 June investigation account describes a March 2026 LiteLLM incident. Their inclusion in this newly expanded preparation does not make them November events. The financing, annualization and incident qualifications remain part of the respective evidence records.

The earlier frozen files retain their original exact bytes. The correction is an explicit change in identity accounting, not a disappearance of the educational subset or a retraction of its documented model-scoring workflow. Future change logs should report family identity corrections separately from newly added source observations.

[research_gap] No prior published edition exists in this ledger, so a week-over-week market trend is not estimable from these records. The first publishable comparison will need an actual frozen predecessor, a current source cutoff, a claim-level change list and disclosure of whether each change is a new event, a newly captured older source, a corrected scope or a reclassified identity. Scheduled dates, package preparation and website visibility should be reported separately from archive confirmation.

[method] Correction accounting distinguishes claim meaning from the evidence binding used to establish it. The 26 old IDs remain candidate records with earlier positive reviews and later negative/context-reconciliation history. Their new IDs carry fresh author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content receipts. This report uses only the approved replacements. Original source publication, capture and earlier review dates are preserved; the repair does not change the frozen 250-case diagnostic sample, its truth labels, predictions or results, and does not complete either launch audit.

## 3. Market definition, structure and provider categories

[method] Operational market definition: an AI data lab or human-feedback supplier is included here when an approved public source documents an offering that creates, collects, annotates, curates, validates or evaluates data or executable tasks used in AI development. The category includes services, participant access, software-assisted workflows and environment products. Inclusion means that the scoped offering meets this research definition. It does not assert a legal industry classification, a minimum revenue level, independent ownership, a named downstream contribution or an exclusive business focus.

[analysis] Participant access is one delivery category. Prolific offers selected participants and distinguishes platform access from managed collection; Terac offers verified-expert access with an expert-payout-plus-platform-fee model. Handshake’s contractor agreement describes a Human Data Services program whose onboarding does not guarantee a project. These are useful starting points when the buyer can own task design and acceptance, but the degree of project management and supplier responsibility must be read in the contract. Access to a qualified population is not the same deliverable as an accepted dataset.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.platform-managed), [candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.ai-taskers), [candidate.cohort5.terac.expert-supply-offer](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.expert-supply-offer), [candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model), [candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.human-data-program](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.human-data-program), [candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.matching-no-guarantee](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.handshake_ai.matching-no-guarantee)

[analysis] Managed data production combines personnel, instructions, tools and review. Appen describes expert alignment and evaluation; Sama describes an in-house workforce and human-verified data services; iMerit describes expert review and client audits; DataForce describes expert/native-speaker matching and adjudication. These examples are grouped by disclosed responsibility, not presumed equivalence. A managed-service comparison should identify who writes the rubric, who employs or contracts with contributors, who owns correction work and who can reject a disputed final unit.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.offering](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.offering), [candidate.cohort2.sama.data-offering](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.sama.data-offering), [candidate.cohort2.sama.employee-delivery](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.sama.employee-delivery), [candidate.cohort2.imerit.review-gates](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.imerit.review-gates), [candidate.cohort2.dataforce.selection-adjudication](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.dataforce.selection-adjudication)

[analysis] Licensed data products are a different procurement path. Snorkel describes non-exclusive dataset and environment products refreshed quarterly; Mercor, Surge, Datacurve and Invisible advertise prebuilt or ready-to-license collections. Defined.ai explicitly separates marketplace or third-party proprietary datasets from new collection and services. The relevant comparison is therefore version, license, overlap with existing training data, refresh entitlement and fitness on the buyer’s task. A catalog listing does not establish the right to redistribute every source component or the availability of exclusive data.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.snorkel_ai.data-series), [candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.catalog), [candidate.supplier.surge_ai.ots](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.surge_ai.ots), [candidate.cohort4.datacurve.ots-datasets](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.datacurve.ots-datasets), [candidate.cohort2.invisible.data-catalog](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.invisible.data-catalog), [candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.defined_ai.marketplace-separation)

[analysis] Environment builders deliver executable tasks, state and reward logic. Abundant describes turning customer workflows into Foundry environments; Refresh describes simulated coding and computer-use worlds; Bespoke describes company-scale simulations; HackerRank Bench offers resettable repository environments and hidden verifiers; Prime Intellect couples environments with managed training and compute. A buyer should separate environment authorship from hosted execution and post-training services. Portability, reset determinism, observability, judge calibration and maintenance obligations can matter as much as the number of tasks in a package.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.abundant_ai.foundry-customer-offer), [candidate.cohort4.refresh.simulation-environments](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.refresh.simulation-environments), [candidate.cohort5.bespoke_labs.simulation-scope](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.bespoke_labs.simulation-scope), [candidate.cohort5.hackerrank.rl-package](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.hackerrank.rl-package), [candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.managed-training-platform](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.managed-training-platform)

[analysis] Evaluation and safety services may use expert data without selling a general annotation workforce. Giskard offers dynamic evaluation data and adaptive attacks; Alinia describes policy judges and comparison with customer experts; Trajectory describes expert-discovered safety attacks and automated testing of known attacks. Their documented value propositions concern discovery, assessment and iteration. A procurement team should specify whether the output is a test dataset, a report, an integrated judge, a remediation cycle or a continuous service before comparing prices or treating these providers as substitutes for custom training-data production.

[analysis] Engineering teams and talent programs can occupy a distinct contractual position. A.Team offers builders for environment and evaluation engineering. G2i advertises engineering data programs and dual-developer review, yet its inspected human-data terms limit the service to talent acquisition and disclaim responsibility for candidate work. Proximal’s MSA instead keeps responsibility for subcontracted services with Proximal. These documents demonstrate why a shared engineering capability label cannot establish who warrants the final artifact. The contract should identify the accountable supplier, the accepted output and the path for defects.

Dataloop documents human/AI feedback nodes; Datasaur combines automated NLP pre-labeling with human verification; Kili lets customer specialists author and judge post-training examples and introduces external partners; V7 Darwin supports multistage workflows and advertised specialist access. These products can support human-data production without establishing that the software company directly employs the annotators or warrants every add-on’s delivery. Compare platform controls, expert access and managed-service responsibility as separate line items.

Encord offers physical-AI, multimodal and LLM annotation with role matching; APTO lists image, video, LiDAR, text and audio; Shaip describes credentialed professionals for healthcare, legal, finance and code preference work. A modality claim does not establish specialist expertise, and a credential claim does not establish coverage in every language or format. Buyers should intersect the required domain, locale, tool environment and output type, rather than add separate broad claims into an unsupported statement of complete coverage.

[method] Provider categories are overlapping analyst groupings of documented offerings, not mutually exclusive market segments. A supplier can appear in several use-case comparisons without being counted several times. A brand, product, division or contractor platform is not automatically a separate corporate supplier. RWS/TrainAI, Welocalize/Welo Data, HackerRank/Bench and Alegion/SanctifAI retain the scoped identity disclosed in their records. Historical aliases remain searchable without inventing a new ownership transaction or a second supplier.

[analysis] Named delivery strengthens the ability to ask focused diligence questions, but evidence type still matters. DataForce’s IBM case, SuperAnnotate’s Databricks case, Aya Data’s Cydar case and Keymakr’s SeeChange case are provider-authored descriptions with different artifacts and dates. They are not matched outcome trials. A supplier without a named public case in this graph may have confidential deliveries; a supplier with one has not thereby demonstrated superior quality. Disclosure completeness and provider performance are distinct objects of study.

The report instead makes a narrower, falsifiable judgment: supplier comparison should follow responsibility and deliverable structure. CrowdAgent describes routing and hidden-gold aggregation; LMCrowd describes staged model-label purchasing. Neither establishes that a named supplier currently implements those workflows or achieves their results. For managed work, compare responsibility for guidelines, routing, escalation, independent acceptance and full cost. For a method implementation, compare the exact data, models, selection rules and held-out checks. A paper-to-practice connection can suggest questions without becoming an unsupported supplier-contribution edge.

## 4. Technical landscape: from supervision to executable evaluation

[method] This chapter separates stages that are often collapsed into RLHF: source collection; task and rubric authoring; demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning; outcome ratings, preference pairs or ranked sets; reward or judge construction; policy optimization; executable environment design; evaluation; and documentation. The reviewed-work atlas below summarizes approved observations from exact inspected manifestations. A paper’s work identity counts once even when several versions exist. Bounded full_source review covers methods plus main results or worked examples and limitations; it does not claim all appendices, proofs, raw data or experiments were reproduced.

[analysis] Classical human-preference pipelines expose several independent design choices. The original trajectory-comparison study alternates interaction, human clip comparisons and reward fitting. The summarization study uses comparison-trained rewards and PPO with a KL penalty. InstructGPT ranks sets of responses and uses a separate unlabelled prompt pool for PPO. These are not merely different names for pairwise annotation: they differ in task construction, candidate sampling, comparison independence and the distribution exposed to optimization. A data purchase should preserve those distinctions in its manifest.

Evidence IDs: [cohort2.claim.humanprefs.async-method](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.humanprefs.async-method), [cohort2.claim.humanprefs.clip-labels](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.humanprefs.clip-labels), [cohort3.claim.summarize.pipeline](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.summarize.pipeline), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.unlabelled-ppo-inputs](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.unlabelled-ppo-inputs)

[analysis] Preference optimization changes the training interface, rather than erasing data requirements. DPO fits a direct objective without a separate reward-model/RL loop; IPO studies a direct squared-loss formulation under a narrower experimental setting; ORPO combines chosen-response likelihood and odds-ratio loss without a frozen reference; KTO accepts desirable/undesirable labels. KTO experiments often transform existing pairs, so support for a binary interface is not evidence that all reported data were independently collected as binary judgments. Method comparison must retain label origin, model scale, candidate distribution and evaluation protocol.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.dpo.direct-policy-objective](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.dpo.direct-policy-objective), [cohort2.claim.ipo.identity-objective](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.ipo.identity-objective), [cohort2.claim.ipo.lm-scaling-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.ipo.lm-scaling-limit), [cohort2.claim.orpo.monolithic-loss](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.orpo.monolithic-loss), [cohort2.claim.orpo.reference-free](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.orpo.reference-free), [cohort2.claim.kto.binary-signal](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.kto.binary-signal), [cohort2.claim.kto.paired-source-transformation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.kto.paired-source-transformation)

[analysis] Selection methods consume a candidate budget that is absent from a final retained-pair count. RAFT retains a high-reward fraction; statistical rejection sampling generates 64 candidates and subsamples eight in its standard experiment; SimPO’s instruct setting selects highest/lowest PairRM scores from five candidates; SPPO also uses five responses per prompt in its experiment. Their results cannot be explained by final training-row counts alone. A reproducible data and compute comparison should count generated candidates, judge calls, retained examples, rejected items, training updates and evaluation calls separately.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.raft.batch-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.raft.batch-selection), [cohort5.claim.rso.budget](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.rso.budget), [cohort5.claim.simpo.instruct-data](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.simpo.instruct-data), [cohort5.claim.sppo.selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.sppo.selection)

[analysis] Process supervision targets intermediate steps, but step granularity and validation still differ. Let’s Verify Step by Step evaluates selection from a fixed generator and flags a large-scale comparison confound; Step-DPO contrasts next steps conditioned on earlier correct steps and warns that correct final answers can conceal bad intermediate reasoning; PRIME learns an online implicit process reward from outcome supervision. A buyer should distinguish human step labels from model-localized errors and from token rewards derived indirectly from final outcomes. None of these method labels alone proves faithful reasoning.

Evidence IDs: [cohort2.claim.process.fixed-generator-scope](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.process.fixed-generator-scope), [cohort2.claim.process.large-comparison-confound](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.process.large-comparison-confound), [cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-objective](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-objective), [cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-limit), [cohort8.claim.prime.online-prm](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.prime.online-prm), [cohort8.claim.prime.token-reward](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.prime.token-reward)

[analysis] Optimization papers also change normalization, sampling and infrastructure assumptions. DAPO filters all-correct or all-incorrect sampled groups and changes clipping and token aggregation; Dr. GRPO analyzes response-length and reward-standard-deviation biases; GSPO clips sequence ratios; VAPO adds value pretraining and length-adaptive advantages. These are specific recipes under their inspected experiments, not evidence of a universally best algorithm or a provider’s operational advantage. A buyer of training services should ask which recipe, reward definition, sampling budget and failure controls are actually implemented.

Evidence IDs: [cohort8.claim.dapo.dynamic-sampling](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.dapo.dynamic-sampling), [cohort8.claim.dapo.clip-higher](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.dapo.clip-higher), [cohort8.claim.dapo.token-loss](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.dapo.token-loss), [cohort8.claim.drgrpo.length-bias](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.drgrpo.length-bias), [cohort8.claim.drgrpo.difficulty-bias](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.drgrpo.difficulty-bias), [cohort8.claim.gspo.sequence-ratio](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.gspo.sequence-ratio), [cohort8.claim.vapo.value-pretraining](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.vapo.value-pretraining), [cohort8.claim.vapo.length-adaptive](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.vapo.length-adaptive)

[analysis] Test-time adaptation needs a different evaluation contract. TTRL uses agreement with a sampled consensus as reward without target ground-truth labels; ReliableTTRL distinguishes population-majority error from finite-rollout variation; SelectTTRL fixes a selection rule without target answers but uses a separately labeled calibration set. Reporting only a final score hides adaptation data access and evaluation-budget differences. A fair comparison should state which test questions drive updates, which labels enter calibration, the total rollout budget, checkpoint-selection rule and whether every target question remains in the denominator.

Evidence IDs: [cohort8.claim.ttrl.consensus-reward](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.ttrl.consensus-reward), [cohort8.claim.ttrl.test-adaptation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.ttrl.test-adaptation), [cohort8.claim.reliablettrl.error-types](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.reliablettrl.error-types), [cohort8.claim.reliablettrl.final-checkpoint](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.reliablettrl.final-checkpoint), [cohort8.claim.selectttrl.calibration](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.selectttrl.calibration), [cohort8.claim.selectttrl.all-evaluated](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.selectttrl.all-evaluated)

[analysis] Synthetic and hybrid pipelines require stage-level lineage. Constitutional AI mixes human helpfulness with model harmlessness labels; ToolBench combines expert seed examples with ChatGPT instruction and trajectory generation; RLAIF-V uses model claim checking while its evaluation references include human corrections; Llama 3 collects new annotations and synthetic data across rounds. The practical requirement is a manifest identifying generator, prompt, seed material, selection model, correction roles and independent evaluation. A statement that humans were involved somewhere cannot establish that a particular training target is human-authored.

Evidence IDs: [cohort2.claim.constitutional.hybrid-label-origin](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.constitutional.hybrid-label-origin), [cohort4.claim.toolbench.synthetic-pipeline](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.toolbench.synthetic-pipeline), [cohort3.claim.rlaifv.claim-feedback](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.rlaifv.claim-feedback), [cohort3.claim.rlaifv.evaluation-human-proprietary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.rlaifv.evaluation-human-proprietary), [cohort5.claim.llama3.rounds](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.llama3.rounds)

[analysis] Executable evaluation spans different abstractions. HumanEval checks short Python functions; SWE-bench checks issue-resolution patches; WebArena combines semantic and state checks; OSWorld uses desktop state evaluators; τ-bench checks database outcomes under interaction policies. Agents can receive different observation modes, budgets and simulator affordances. A single leaderboard column cannot remove these differences. The comparison should first ask whether the measured task and environment resemble the buyer’s deployment, then assess whether the scoring protocol detects the failures the buyer cares about.

Evidence IDs: [cohort4.claim.humaneval.task-construction](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.humaneval.task-construction), [candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.swebench.regression-test-scoring), [cohort2.claim.webarena.hybrid-evaluation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.webarena.hybrid-evaluation), [cohort4.claim.osworld.executable-outcome-judge](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.osworld.executable-outcome-judge), [cohort4.claim.taubench.interactive-environment](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.taubench.interactive-environment)

[analysis] Research and professional-work benchmarks add substantial human design and review labor. RE-Bench records expert runs with tools; ScienceAgentBench uses subject-matter validation and separate execution verification; PaperBench aggregates binary rubric leaves and prohibits use of original authors’ code; TheAgentCompany records task-creation effort but lacks a professional human comparison in that iteration. These benchmarks make particular research activities observable, but their human baselines, time budgets and allowed resources differ. They cannot establish a general percentage of jobs that an agent can perform.

Evidence IDs: [cohort6.claim.rebench.human-count](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.rebench.human-count), [cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools), [cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.human-validation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.human-validation), [cohort6.claim.paperbench.rubric](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.paperbench.rubric), [cohort6.claim.paperbench.original-code-rule](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.paperbench.original-code-rule), [cohort6.claim.agentcompany.curation-labor](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.agentcompany.curation-labor), [repair.binding.v1.cohort6.claim.agentcompany.human-baseline-limit](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.cohort6.claim.agentcompany.human-baseline-limit)

[analysis] Reward hacking and contamination should be studied as separate mechanisms. A learned reward can be overoptimized while human preference worsens; a program can pass supplied assertions by hard-coding tested inputs; a reasoning monitor can lose recall under direct optimization pressure; a public benchmark can be detected in training only under particular access and watermark assumptions. These examples motivate separate checks for objective misspecification, verifier gaming, monitor adaptation and training/test exposure. They do not establish the incidence of those failures in any provider’s current production service.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.summarize.overoptimization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.summarize.overoptimization), [cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.mbpp.test-overfit), [cohort7.claim.monitor.optimization](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.monitor.optimization), [cohort8.claim.stamp.access-timing](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.stamp.access-timing), [cohort8.claim.stamp.paired-design](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.stamp.paired-design)

[analysis] Feedback-format comparison — ordinal ratings, rankings and binary signals preserve different information. HelpSteer2’s attribute ratings can retain multiple dimensions; InstructGPT’s ranked sets relate several responses under one prompt; Llama 2 adds preference strength; KTO can use one desirable/undesirable output. Converting all of them to binary pairs can discard attribute structure or strength and create correlated observations. The buyer should decide which information is required by the intended objective before paying for annotation. The reviewed studies do not establish one universally most efficient format, and the matched disagreement study specifically cautions against assuming paired preferences are inherently less ambiguous.

Evidence IDs: [next.claim.helpsteer2.attributes](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.helpsteer2.attributes), [candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.instructgpt.human-ranking-sets), [cohort5.claim.llama2.preference](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.llama2.preference), [cohort2.claim.kto.binary-signal](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.claim.kto.binary-signal), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.agreement-not-superiority)

[analysis] Feedback-format comparison — rationale text and process labels answer different questions. The natural-language-feedback study uses author-written feedback to select refinements by embedding similarity; Innodata describes explanatory reasons for response scores; Step-DPO localizes the next erroneous step; DeepSeek-R1-Zero uses final accuracy and format rewards without a neural process reward. A rationale can be useful context without being a validated causal explanation or a correct intermediate proof. Procurement should distinguish the requested text artifact, its validation target and whether downstream training actually consumes it. These examples do not show that longer reasoning or more explanation is always better.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.human-feedback](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.human-feedback), [cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.selection), [candidate.cohort3.innodata.explanatory-feedback](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort3.innodata.explanatory-feedback), [cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-objective](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.stepdpo.step-objective), [cohort5.claim.deepseekr1.zero-reward](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekr1.zero-reward)

[analysis] Distribution comparison — offline preferences and current-policy rollouts can differ even when the file schema is identical. SLiC-HF notes mismatch between off-policy human-feedback data and SFT decodes; WPO reweights preference losses using current-policy response weights; REBEL permits a fixed or current-policy response distribution but samples both responses from the current policy in its described experiments. These methods make the candidate-generation distribution a material part of the recipe. A licensed preference dataset should therefore identify generating models, sampling settings and collection period, and a training-service proposal should explain whether fresh responses or labels are required.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.slichf.distribution-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.slichf.distribution-limit), [cohort5.claim.wpo.weights](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.wpo.weights), [cohort5.claim.rebel.distribution](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.rebel.distribution), [cohort5.claim.rebel.online-experiment](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.rebel.online-experiment)

[analysis] Objective comparison — a scalar reward is a modeling choice, not a property guaranteed by human judgment. SPPO explicitly uses a two-player constant-sum preference game rather than requiring one transitive scalar ordering; WPO’s conceptual labeling construction assumes no conflicting pairs for a prompt; the instruction-tuning disagreement experiment observes task-dependent ambiguity. The analytical lesson is to state the aggregation assumptions and preserve counterexamples before fitting a reward. This does not prove that scalar models are inappropriate in every task; it identifies a condition to test when disagreements are central to the buyer’s use case.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.sppo.game](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.sppo.game), [cohort5.claim.wpo.assumption](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.wpo.assumption), [cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.disagreement.instance-disagreement)

[analysis] Budget comparison — optimization improvements can be inseparable from sample selection and validation conditions. Llama 3 rejection sampling generates 10–30 outputs per human-annotation prompt; DeepSeekMath samples 64 outputs per question in its described run; TTRL uses 64 voting responses and a 32-response training subsample. These are different compute and information budgets. A comparison based on retained examples, final model size or optimizer name alone is incomplete. Report total generations, token caps, judge calls and human checking, then distinguish training expenditure from evaluation expenditure. No cross-paper cost-normalized winner is computed here.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.llama3.sampling](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.llama3.sampling), [cohort5.claim.deepseekmath.sampling-budget](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekmath.sampling-budget), [repair.binding.ten.v1.cohort8.claim.ttrl.vote-then-sample](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.ten.v1.cohort8.claim.ttrl.vote-then-sample)

[analysis] Systems comparison — orchestration describes how computation moves, not whether feedback is valid. OpenRLHF uses separate rollout/training roles with vLLM and DeepSpeed and limits the inspected paper’s support to language models. HybridFlow routes data between parallel layouts and generally executes colocated roles sequentially to avoid contention or memory failures. A platform’s architectural support is therefore separate from a proof of label provenance, a task’s reward soundness or the performance of a trained model. For a systems purchase, ask for reproducible resource and data-flow measurements under the actual recipe while auditing feedback quality through a different protocol.

Evidence IDs: [cohort8.claim.openrlhf.vllm-deepspeed](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.openrlhf.vllm-deepspeed), [cohort8.claim.openrlhf.language-scope](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.openrlhf.language-scope), [cohort8.claim.hybridflow.transfer-protocols](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.hybridflow.transfer-protocols), [cohort8.claim.hybridflow.general-sequential](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.hybridflow.general-sequential)

[analysis] Curation comparison — dataset selection can change task composition as well as nominal quality. AlpaGasus retains a model-scored subset of Alpaca and flags disproportionate removal of keyword-defined coding examples; DCLM’s classifier retains a top-scoring fraction under a defined positive/negative training set; DataComp permits filtered size to vary under fixed samples-seen compute. The defensible interpretation is that filters select a distribution according to their targets. A buyer should inspect what was removed and the resulting task mix, rather than infer that every discarded example was objectively bad or that a smaller selected set is universally better.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.alpagasus.selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.alpagasus.selection), [cohort3.claim.alpagasus.skill-balance](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.alpagasus.skill-balance), [cohort3.claim.dclm.quality-filter](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dclm.quality-filter), [cohort3.claim.datacomp.controlled-design](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.datacomp.controlled-design)

[analysis] Evaluation comparison — win rate depends on who judges, what counts as a win and how ties are handled. The natural-language-feedback experiment counts ties as half a win; LIMA reports separate wins, ties and losses against dated responses; Llama 3 excludes slightly-better ratings from wins; RSO uses a three-rater majority. These figures cannot be pooled into a common preference advantage without the underlying protocol. A pilot should freeze the response population, judge rubric, blinding, tie rule and aggregation before comparing candidates, and report enough raw counts to reconstruct the stated metric.

Evidence IDs: [cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.test-protocol](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.languagefeedback.test-protocol), [cohort3.claim.lima.dated-human-comparison](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.lima.dated-human-comparison), [cohort5.claim.llama3.human-win](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.llama3.human-win), [cohort5.claim.rso.human-protocol](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.rso.human-protocol)

[analysis] Human-baseline comparison — the reference population and tools define the comparison. MMLU’s approximate expert level is an estimate rather than a measured panel across all subjects; RE-Bench allows human internet and LLM use; VisualWebArena avoids assigning task creators to their own tasks; WebShop gives humans HTML observations while models use simplified text. These are substantive design choices. A claim that an agent exceeds humans should identify which humans, prior task exposure, allowed tools, time limits and observation mode. The reviewed record does not support a general human-versus-AI capability ranking.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.paperfull.mmlu.estimated-expert-baseline](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.mmlu.estimated-expert-baseline), [cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.rebench.human-tools), [cohort4.claim.visualwebarena.human-separation](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.visualwebarena.human-separation), [cohort4.claim.webshop.observation-comparability](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.webshop.observation-comparability)

[analysis] Contamination comparison — tests detect particular kinds of overlap. MBPP’s normalized line-overlap analysis concerns eligible reference-program lines; BIG-bench’s canary is an intended training-exclusion signal; DeepSeekMath removes benchmark n-grams under its stated matching rules; STAMP requires pre-release watermarking and token-probability access. None of these procedures proves all forms of semantic or strategy-level independence. Buyers using public tasks should record exposure assumptions and run private or freshly authored holdouts where appropriate, while acknowledging that private construction also needs verification and rights review.

Evidence IDs: [cohort4.claim.mbpp.overlap-check](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.mbpp.overlap-check), [cohort4.claim.bigbench.contamination-canary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.claim.bigbench.contamination-canary), [cohort5.claim.deepseekmath.decontamination](evidence.html#assertion-cohort5.claim.deepseekmath.decontamination), [cohort8.claim.stamp.access-timing](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.stamp.access-timing), [cohort8.claim.stamp.one-sided-test](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.stamp.one-sided-test)

[analysis] Generalization comparison — different kinds of difficulty should remain separate. GPQA explicitly disclaims representativeness of scientific practice; HLE states that a high score alone would not demonstrate autonomous research; ScienceAgentBench selects Python partly because of annotator familiarity; RE-Bench warns that short clear tasks with supplied resources are unlike open-ended research. A buyer should use these benchmarks to locate specific weaknesses and design target-workflow tests. They do not justify extrapolating an exam score or a short-horizon optimization result into complete professional capability, employment substitution or general intelligence.

Evidence IDs: [cohort6.claim.gpqa.representativeness-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.gpqa.representativeness-limit), [cohort6.claim.hle.capability-limit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.hle.capability-limit), [cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.python-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.scienceagentbench.python-selection), [cohort6.claim.rebench.representativeness](evidence.html#assertion-cohort6.claim.rebench.representativeness)

[analysis] The additional annotation literature changes how the earlier technical methods should be read. Snow’s simplified temporal task and Gilardi’s agreed-human subset show that the reference population can change a model-versus-human comparison. HelpSteer2’s filtering changes the retained label population, while the label-error study shows that even corrected benchmark labels remain uncertain. A method comparison therefore needs three explicit objects: the items admitted, the rule defining reference truth and the items excluded before the headline result. This report treats those as experimental scope, rather than evidence of a universal labor or model advantage.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Consent in Crisis: The Rapid Decline of the AI Data Commons. The audited corpus sources are C4, RefinedWeb and Dolma. The head sample unions the top 2,000 domains by token count from each corpus into 3,950 domains. The random sample draws 10,000 domains from the 10,136,147-domain intersection and uses a random 2,000-domain subset for human annotation. [sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Data Cards: Purposeful and Transparent Dataset Documentation for Responsible AI. Data Cards document critical dataset information across its life cycle and allow tailored templates rather than one fixed schema for every dataset. The design principles organize cards into self-contained modular sections and support multiple granularities and content types. The authors develop a participatory workshop approach that engages cross-functional stakeholders when creating transparent dataset metadata schemas. In the reported cases, Google Docs card templates supported collaboration but field-level iteration caused fragmentation and limited automation of collection. Reading boundary: Framework design; flexibility does not establish that a particular card is complete or accurate.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Datasheets for Datasets. The authors propose documenting a dataset’s motivation, composition, collection process and recommended uses. The questions and workflow were refined over roughly two years with multiple rounds of feedback. The paper states that datasheets alone are not a complete mitigation for unwanted societal bias or potential dataset harms. The authors intend datasheet creation to involve reflective human documentation rather than an automated creation process. For infrequently changing datasets, the authors recommend accompanying updated dataset versions with updated datasheets. The proposed collection-process documentation asks dataset creators to identify collection participants and their compensation. Reading boundary: Subsequent paragraphs describe example datasheets, product teams, researcher/practitioner/policy comments and legal feedback; this is author-reported development, not a controlled effectiveness trial.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Documenting Large Webtext Corpora: A Case Study on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus. The contamination analysis uses exact matches normalized for capitalization and punctuation and treats multi-component benchmark inputs separately. The authors leave quantification or removal of likely personally identifiable and copyrighted text in C4 for future work. C4 is derived from the April2019 Common Crawl snapshot with English identification and content filters, including a blocklist. Reading boundary: Exact input overlap does not alone establish that a benchmark label was present or that a trained model memorized it.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models. The evaluation generates three pools of 200,000 samples, each sample 256 tokens long. The study identifies 604 unique memorized examples among its 1,800 selected candidates, reported as a 33.5% aggregate true-positive rate. For each of 18 generation-strategy/metric configurations, the study selects 100 samples from the metric’s top 1,000. The paper distinguishes training-data extraction of verbatim examples from inversion that reconstructs representative examples. Reading boundary: GPT-2 XL (1.5B parameters); strategies are top-n empty-sequence sampling, temperature sampling and Internet-conditioned sampling. [sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Minority Reports: Balancing Cost and Quality in Ground Truth Data Annotation. The pruning rule retains assignments involving unseen workers or tasks; otherwise it prunes when estimated minority-report probability exceeds a fixed threshold. Simulation quality is measured by comparing post-pruning majority votes against the counterfactual unpruned majority, using yes/no accuracy and F1. The paper defines a minority report as an annotator response that differs from the final majority-vote consensus for an image-crop question. The discussion cautions that RLHF ranked preferences can have high variability without a clear majority or a single notion of ground truth. Reading boundary: Prediction uses previously observed assignments and is recalibrated over time; a pruning decision is not a general worker competence judgment.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: Sources of Disagreement in Data for LLM Instruction Tuning. On the full human dataset, quadratic-weighted kappa is 0.48 for SINGLE ratings and 0.43 for PREFERENCE combined scores; the authors find no evidence in this setup that preference annotation is easier or less ambiguous. Across the two human task formulations, the study reports instance-level disagreement correlation R=0.2 and ambiguity-set overlap 0.25, despite using the same annotators and data points. The zero-shot annotation experiment uses four instruction-tuned models from 1B to 8B; the 1B model has no reported human-label correlation, while the other three have correlation in 0.2–0.25. The human experiment selects720 Anthropic context/two-response instances, evenly split between helpful and harmless, and recruits 33 graduate-course annotators to perform both individual 1–5 quality ratings and paired preference/magnitude tasks. Reading boundary: This is a result for the studied population, generic quality instructions and sample; it does not establish all disagreement as noise.

The initial audit covers 44 instruction/alignment finetuning collections comprising 1,858 individual datasets selected by experts for widespread use; overlapping datasets are intentionally not deduplicated to preserve collection design choices. The license protocol searches for creator-attributable licenses explicitly applying to data, distinguishes them from code licenses, and records permitted-use, attribution and share-alike categories with the strictest feature across multiple licenses. The provenance audit combines linked public metadata, human legal-expert annotation and GPT-4-assisted annotation; its topic annotation uses GPT-4 on a sample of 100 examples for up to 10 topics. Recorded worker interviews are transcribed, accompanied by debriefing reports and coded using both descriptive categories and literature-informed theoretical categories. [sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Documentation, labor and evidence quality: “Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work”: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI. COVID-era video/phone interviews prevent workflow shadowing and contextual inquiry; the findings are self-reported practices in high-stakes projects, with sampling and gender-distribution limitations. The study groups cascades into physical-world brittleness, inadequate application-domain expertise, conflicting reward systems and poor cross-organizational documentation. Between May and July 2020, the authors conduct semi-structured interviews with 53 high-stakes AI practitioners: 23 in India, 16 in the US and 14 in East/West African countries, using purposive and snowball recruitment. The authors report that 92% of their 53 interview participants experienced at least one data cascade, defined as compounding data-related events producing negative downstream effects and technical debt. Reading boundary: Percentages are coded self-reports in the selected interview sample and are not population prevalence.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Feedback, rewards and policy optimization: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Preferences. IPO is an identity-mapping special case of ΨPO that learns directly from preferences without a reward-modeling stage or the Bradley-Terry pairwise-to-pointwise assumption. The sampled-preference comparisons use three-action bandits, softmax parameterizations, 18,000 Adam steps and ten seeds; reported curves include means and 95% confidence intervals. The paper leaves scaling IPO experiments to more complex settings, including training language models on human preference data, to future work. IPO optimizes an empirical squared loss on the policy/reference log-likelihood ratio of preferred versus dispreferred actions, targeting one-half the inverse regularization coefficient. Reading boundary: These are illustrative bandit experiments, not LLM benchmark results.

[sourced_fact] Reviewed-work atlas — Feedback, rewards and policy optimization: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale. DAPO separates lower and upper clipping ranges, increasing the upper range while retaining the lower range to encourage low-probability-token exploration. Dynamic sampling oversamples and excludes prompts whose sampled response group has all-correct or all-incorrect answers, continuing until the effective batch is filled. Soft overlong punishment adds a length-dependent penalty to correctness rewards within a configured interval near the generation limit. DAPO aggregates the policy loss over tokens across the sampled batch, replacing equal weighting of response-level average losses. Reading boundary: Mechanism described in the selected version; the candidate makes no universal entropy or quality guarantee.

The method asynchronously alternates environment interaction/policy updates, eliciting human trajectory-pair comparisons, and supervised fitting of a learned reward predictor. Human raters compare 1-2 second trajectory clips and may prefer either clip, mark them equal, or mark them incomparable; incomparable judgments are omitted from the comparison database. The evaluation separates real human comparisons, synthetic oracle comparisons derived from environment reward, and RL with the real reward. Real-human MuJoCo and Atari curves each represent a single run. In the offline-only reward-predictor ablation, optimizing a predictor fitted only at the start can exploit incomplete reward estimates, including Pong policies that avoid losses without scoring. Reading boundary: Curve averaging differs by condition: five runs for other MuJoCo curves and three for other Atari curves.

The authors propose using inference-engine sequence likelihoods directly as a possible way to avoid old-policy likelihood recomputation in the training engine. The GSPO comparison begins with a cold-start model fine-tuned from Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base and evaluates AIME24, LiveCodeBench from October 2024 to February 2025, and CodeForces. GSPO clips entire responses, with length normalization intended to control ratio variance and numerical range across response lengths.
