[analysis] Workforce arrangement changes the questions to ask. Sama describes full-time in-house delivery; TELUS Digital lists several workforce modes; Alegion describes workforce partners; Scale describes BPOs and proprietary platforms; isahit describes self-employed onboarding. These descriptions cannot establish legal status or worker experience across jurisdictions. For a project, record the contracting entity, subcontracting chain, training obligation, supervision, payment authority and appeal channel rather than assume the same conditions from a shared annotation label.

[analysis] Compensation disclosures concern different units and conditions. Prolific publishes permitted minimum and recommended participant hourly rates; Handshake puts amount, type and timing in project invitations; Humans in the Loop uses supervisor-approved delivered units; Snorkel processes accepted contributions weekly; micro1 states a twice-monthly schedule. These are rules or schedules, not comparable realized wages. Any labor analysis should count qualification, waiting, revisions, rejections and administrative time separately and retain the project’s currency and payment basis.

[analysis] Sensitive-content and monitoring rules deserve operational evidence. Scale describes notice, the ability to decline and wellness resources; Toloka requires disclosure and acknowledgement before labeling; the dated Welo case describes informed consent; Invisible discloses keystroke, screenshot and webcam collection with possible access consequences if declined. These sources describe different settings. They do not prove that every worker could safely refuse, obtained support or experienced proportionate monitoring. A buyer should request project notices, escalation handling and aggregate worker-feedback evidence without seeking unnecessary personal records.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.sensitive-content), [candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.toloka.sensitive-content), [candidate.cohort2.welocalize.sensitive-content-consent](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.welocalize.sensitive-content-consent), [candidate.cohort2.invisible.work-monitoring](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.invisible.work-monitoring)

[analysis] Labor research has its own sampling limits. The Data-Production Dispositif combines interviews, observation and instruction-document analysis in specific Latin American settings; the Latin American labor article states that unknown platform-population boundaries limit statistical representativeness; the requester-proxy study limits its conclusions to US requester perspectives and self-reports. These studies illuminate mechanisms and research questions. They should not become global percentages, a census of all workers or evidence that a named supplier currently practices every behavior described.

[research_gap] Important labor unknowns remain: independently measured effective pay, qualification rejection and appeal outcomes, subcontractor payment reconciliation, harmful-content exposure, contributor retention and the relation between monitoring and acceptance. The public-source corpus does not resolve these for the covered market. Research can progress through consented worker studies, project-level anonymized logs and comparable definitions, while avoiding inference from registered pools or recruitment advertisements.

[analysis] Disagreement routing should distinguish uncertainty from error. Experts Rise uses cross-model entropy to select expert attention, while Inherent Disagreements models multiple interpretations of the same short sentence pairs. CrowdTruth defines mutually dependent consistency scores but leaves broader comparative validation open. The practical choice is whether the task seeks one verifiable answer, a distribution of valid interpretations or a codebook revision. Record that choice before using disagreement to exclude workers, remove items or declare a quality improvement.

[analysis] Instruction design and assistance need separate acceptance checks. The surgical study’s comparison is conditional on instruction richness and project-specific QA; LabelAId’s intervention improves precision within a 34-person study without an equivalence finding on time. Neither supports a general staffing reduction. In a proposed pilot, log instruction revisions, assistance shown, human corrections and downstream acceptance, then inspect whether the intervention changes errors or merely which cases remain. Preserve any effect on contributor effort and disagreement as part of the operating record.

## 8. Commercial evidence and procurement economics

[sourced_fact] Appen — reported revenue. The audited FY2025 statements report consolidated customer-contract revenue of USD 230.774 million for 1 January–31 December 2025, including Appen Global USD 127.874 million and Appen China USD 102.900 million. These geographic operating segments do not isolate expert generative-AI data or the market definition used in this report. The figures are full-year reported revenue, not annualized pace, gross transaction volume, contributor pay or a comparable human-feedback segment across suppliers.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025), [candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025)

[sourced_fact] Proximal — annualized pace. Its 29 September 2026 announcement reports $200 million in annualized revenue. The inspected disclosure does not specify an ISO currency code, annualization window, gross-versus-net basis or revenue split by business line. It is self-reported pace, not an audited annual revenue total, profit, bookings, valuation or contractor payout. No annual recognized-revenue amount is calculated from it in this report.

Evidence IDs: [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure)

[sourced_fact] Scale — cumulative contributor payout. Its FY2025 statement, approved in June 2026, reports nearly $1 billion paid to hundreds of thousands of contributors across more than 150 countries to date. The statement does not define a start/end period or a dollar currency code for that aggregate, and payment reconciliation was not inspected. The number is not annual revenue, annual labor cost, a current paid-active workforce total or a wage estimate.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout)

[sourced_fact] Labelbox — financing and valuation. The 14 October 2026 company announcement reports more than $100 million in Series E financing comprising equity and a credit facility, at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation. The inspected source uses dollar symbols without an explicit ISO currency. The facility is not equity, and financing and valuation are not revenue or evidence of accepted data volume. No implied annual growth or provider-performance score is calculated.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing)

[sourced_fact] Prolific — tariff and reward rules. The captured FAQ states usual platform fees of 42.8% for corporate customers and 33.3% for academic/nonprofit customers, but the bound passage does not explicitly state the percentage denominator. It separately sets minimum participant rewards of GBP 6 or USD 8 per hour and recommends GBP 9 or USD 12, with higher expert compensation recommended. Managed services are custom-priced. These are published rules and tariff disclosures rather than realized earnings, margins or a complete specialist-project quote.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.prolific.fees](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.fees), [candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards)

[sourced_fact] Other disclosed billing units differ. Prime Intellect’s Model Factory terms meter allocated GPU-hours prorated to the second, with rates in the order or platform; personnel post-training needs a separate professional-services order. A.Team lists hourly and other builder-engagement models. Terac describes expert payout plus a platform fee and separately monthly USD payment per verified completion for partnerships. AfterQuery reserves fees to order forms or separate agreements. These documents describe commercial structure, not a comparable price per accepted preference pair or environment.

Evidence IDs: [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.gpu-billing-basis](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.gpu-billing-basis), [candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation), [candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model), [candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model), [candidate.cohort5.terac.partner-payment-basis](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort5.terac.partner-payment-basis), [candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing)

[analysis] The analytical rule is to keep commercial denominators separate. A company-wide annualized rate cannot be divided by a benchmark count to estimate task price; cumulative payouts cannot identify a current take rate; financing cannot measure demand; a broad expert pool cannot be a capacity denominator. The selected disclosures support questions for diligence, not supplier market shares. A defensible future comparison would need the same reporting period, currency, gross/net basis, organizational segment and accepted-unit definition across every included provider.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025), [repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure](evidence.html#assertion-repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure), [candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout), [candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing), [candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool)

[method] Reproducible buyer calculation: accepted-unit cost equals all attributable project cash costs divided by independently accepted units. The numerator should state whether it includes recruitment, qualification, paid training, tool licenses, compute, project management, review, rework and buyer-side acceptance. The denominator should identify the unit: independent judgment, resolved item, trajectory, verified environment, recorded hour or licensed release. This is a proposed accounting method; the report does not insert hypothetical numbers or claim observed costs for suppliers.

[method] Reproducible review calculation: first-pass acceptance equals accepted units on first submission divided by all submitted units; final acceptance equals accepted units after permitted rework divided by all submitted units. Keep attempt, exclusion and unresolved counts. For expert-time projects, report both accepted outputs per paid hour and buyer QA effort per accepted output, without interpreting either as worker wages. For environment projects, separate authoring, maintenance, execution and recurring license costs, and preserve the term of access.

[method] Procurement comparison procedure: issue the same task brief and acceptance rubric, obtain responsibility and rights schedules, run a paid calibration sample, then quote a frozen production scope. Compare totals only after normalizing included review/rework and access terms. Log scope changes as new versions rather than treating a renegotiated specification as supplier underperformance. Proposed service-level thresholds should come from the buyer’s loss tolerance and pilot uncertainty; they are not reported market standards.

[research_gap] The commercial research gap is task-matched economics. This corpus does not supply comparable current contracts, realized gross/net human-data revenue, project margins, cancellation/rework charges or accepted-unit costs across suppliers. Missing financial disclosure is unknown rather than zero. No financial forecast, market-size projection, provider-return model or inferred valuation multiple is warranted by this evidence.

[analysis] Cost comparisons must include the measured boundary. LMCrowd excludes model, prompt and worker selection from its tariff comparison; CrowdAgent holds human annotation proportions rather than all computation or operating cost equal. HelpSteer2 discards about half of collected annotations overall, so accepted responses and purchased ratings have different denominators. Request setup, failed/rejected work, QA, adjudication, model calls, compute and accepted-unit totals explicitly. These studies inform accounting questions; they do not provide current service prices or a cross-provider cost ranking.

Evidence IDs: [cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary), [cohort9.claim.crowdagent.fixed-human-ratios](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.crowdagent.fixed-human-ratios), [cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection](evidence.html#assertion-cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection)

[analysis] Worker-time accounting is also distinct from project billing. The historical MTurk log study produces different work-unit rates under accept-to-submit and temporal-cluster definitions; its task/cluster medians are not median worker wages. Selected plugin users, unknown active effort and noncausal associations constrain inference. For a new project, request consented, task-appropriate compensation and time evidence rather than convert historical platform figures or supplier revenue into a claim about present worker earnings.

## 9. Rights, security, privacy and attribution governance

[analysis] Dataset rights should be modeled as a chain of permissions rather than a single badge. The Data Provenance Initiative distinguishes creator-attributable data licenses from code licenses and explicitly limits itself to best-effort self-reported categorization. Common Pile requires confidence that license information originates with a rights holder. These methods support asking who can grant which rights for each component, transformation and release. They do not establish enforceability or replace project-specific legal review.

Evidence IDs: [cohort3.claim.provenance.data-license-protocol](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.provenance.data-license-protocol), [cohort3.claim.provenance.scope-caveat](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.provenance.scope-caveat), [cohort7.claim.commonpile.licensor](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.commonpile.licensor)

[analysis] Web availability and collection permission are distinct. Consent in Crisis reports inconsistencies between robots.txt signals and terms of service in selected corpora. Documenting C4 recommends documenting included and excluded text and leaves some PII/copyright auditing to future work. FineWeb and Dolma acknowledge residual harmful or sensitive content despite filtering. A buyer should retain capture-time permissions, exclusion rules and removal paths, while treating a crawlable page as a source observation rather than automatic authorization to train or redistribute.

Evidence IDs: [cohort7.claim.consentcrisis.signals](evidence.html#assertion-cohort7.claim.consentcrisis.signals), [cohort8.claim.documentingc4.three-views](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.documentingc4.three-views), [cohort8.claim.documentingc4.future-audit](evidence.html#assertion-cohort8.claim.documentingc4.future-audit), [candidate.paperfull.fineweb.harmful-content-remains](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.paperfull.fineweb.harmful-content-remains), [cohort3.claim.dolma.residual-risk](evidence.html#assertion-cohort3.claim.dolma.residual-risk)

[analysis] License scope can change within a research artifact. AlpacaEval declares different code and data licenses; RewardBench aggregation remains subject to component terms; MathVista retains original image/question copyright and prohibits training use; GAIA asks against public redistribution. The correct unit for diligence is the exact component and use, not a repository’s top-level license string. A restrictive finding does not imply that this report possesses or can redistribute the underlying data.

Evidence IDs: [cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license](evidence.html#assertion-cohort2.dataset.claim.alpacaeval.component-license), [next.claim.rewardbench.terms](evidence.html#assertion-next.claim.rewardbench.terms), [cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.mathvista.terms), [cohort4.dataset.claim.gaia.gate](evidence.html#assertion-cohort4.dataset.claim.gaia.gate)

[analysis] Customer material and website visitor data have different policy boundaries. AfterQuery explicitly excludes processor/service-provider customer processing from its website policy; Mercor excludes its work platform; Label Your Data and LXT describe client-instruction processing; Proximal requires written consent and an executed agreement for generalized-model use of customer material. Obtain the project processing agreement, subprocessors, retention and secondary-use terms. A public policy’s existence does not establish that the proposed delivery is covered by every described safeguard.

Kili’s May 2025 legal notice names MYAI SAS, while its same-date EULA names KILI-TECHNOLOGY SAS under the same Paris registration number; the public inconsistency is unresolved. DDD’s published Terms of Use name DDD Ventures LLC and use investment/real-estate language, so that page does not settle the AI-data contracting identity. iSoftStone’s privacy policy identifies a website-scoped US operator without resolving ultimate ownership or group-wide contracting responsibility. These findings preserve uncertainty rather than invent corporate transactions or additional suppliers.

Evidence IDs: [candidate.cohort6.kili_technology.published-operator-name](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.kili_technology.published-operator-name), [candidate.cohort6.digital_divide_data.legal-page-discrepancy](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.digital_divide_data.legal-page-discrepancy), [candidate.cohort6.isoftstone.website-operator](evidence.html#assertion-candidate.cohort6.isoftstone.website-operator)

Datasaur’s terms contain a free-access deidentified/aggregate improvement exception; Deploy’s terms default to manual Hive Worker review of customer content unless otherwise agreed in writing; Dataocean’s website policy leaves product/project rules to the corresponding services. None of these clauses alone establishes what happened to a particular customer’s records. A buyer should identify the applicable subscription, written exceptions, worker exposure, use permissions and service-specific privacy terms before choosing a delivery path.

For third-party information, the listed conditions include both anonymization before upload and consent agreements. Collection from Tolokers also carries lawful-collection, administering-entity, purpose and policy conditions. These are category-specific platform rules, not a finding that every dataset complies. The linked additional collection guidelines were not separately captured in the reviewed scope.

[analysis] Biometric and authorship metadata deserve separate consent and use records. Toloka’s notice bases identity matching on explicit consent and says refusal can prevent onboarding; it also discloses authorship metadata in some coding deliverables. Turing’s policy lists AI development/training uses of personal information, while Polymath excludes interview voice recordings and transcripts from model training. These statements concern different records and services. Preserve which person, purpose, data type and downstream use each notice covers rather than combine them into a general permission claim.

This report has no common incident-discovery process or equal disclosure window across suppliers. It therefore cannot rank relative security from the presence of that one record or assume that an unrecorded incident never occurred elsewhere.

[analysis] Artifact attribution is nontransitive. Scale’s HelpSteer annotation, Translated’s multilingual role, Prolific’s recruitment case, Toloka’s U-MATH validation and Surge’s GSM8K collection are specific relationships. A paper citing a dataset, an author’s affiliation, a supplier’s general service menu or a benchmark family’s parent link does not establish another supplier contribution. [method] Research governance: the publisher’s public identity discloses applications for paid work at some covered companies, membership in A.Team’s talent network and a separate proposed AI research lab. No profiled company has paid for coverage or is a customer, investor or affiliate of the publisher under that disclosure. External reviewer credit requires consent. This preparation claims actual separate AI source review and will require separate exact-report evidence-auditor and adversarial review; it does not claim human peer review or an external operational certification.

[research_gap] Governance unknowns include project-specific contracts, current assurance-report scopes, removal-request outcomes, consent withdrawals, subprocessor execution and worker appeal effectiveness. These cannot be resolved by treating a top-level license, policy statement or source-content review as an operational audit. Buyer diligence should obtain the relevant documents and test the actual project boundary; future research should record both support and unresolved limitations.

[analysis] Disclosure completeness is an observable governance input, while actual conduct remains a separate question. GIGO audits publication reporting in a selected literature; Who Annotates extracts task-level disclosures with an automated model and a separately adjudicated reference. Both reject equating missing reporting with absent practice. Their results justify asking for training, language proficiency, instructions and reconciliation records. They do not justify ranking a supplier’s ethics or data quality from how many public fields are filled.

[analysis] A documented consent workflow does not finish privacy diligence. WildChat reports an agreement plus secondary confirmation and multilingual PII filtering, yet warns that hashed IPs and request headers can link conversations. The reported process was not independently tested here. For a proposed conversational-data use, examine the exact released fields, linkage routes, permissions and intended population; preserve the difference between a source’s stated control and demonstrated residual risk reduction.

## 10. Buyer decision guides: use cases, pilot designs and acceptance

[method] The following are proposed buyer procedures derived from the reviewed evidence, not reports of completed supplier trials. They do not recommend a universal winner. Each use case states the required deliverable, a candidate responsibility model, a paid pilot and acceptance evidence. The buyer should pre-register critical errors, slices, exclusions, rework limits and decision rules before seeing outputs. Numeric targets should follow the buyer’s risk and uncertainty requirements; no universal accuracy threshold is invented here.

[analysis] Buyer use case 1 — Expert preference data for a specialized assistant: requirement and comparison. Specify prompts, candidate responses, domain credentials, language, independent judgments per item, preference strength and rationale fields. Compare a managed preference program with participant access only after assigning task design, recruitment, adjudication and acceptance. HelpSteer3, HelpSteer2 and InstructGPT show why final pair counts conceal different repetition and aggregation structures.

Freeze the raw-label schema before consensus. Have a separate reviewer inspect disagreements and rejected items without knowing the supplier or initial majority. Keep duplicate prompts and ranked-set expansion identifiable, then hold out a second batch for acceptance.

Reject an unsupported claim that more released pairs necessarily means more independent human evidence.

[analysis] Buyer use case 7 — RAG evaluation and LLM-judge calibration: proposed acceptance and limits. Accept the frozen judge only within the measured scope, documenting thresholds, abstentions and known blind spots. RewardBench 2 warns that reward benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient for strong RLHF training; AlpacaEval warns style can outweigh factuality and that harms are not measured. A judge calibrated on one response population needs renewed testing when the generator or domain changes.

The final purchase decision should state which evidence established suitability and which assumptions remain conditional. Keep unsuccessful pilots and rejected examples in the internal learning record so later comparisons do not inherit survivorship bias.

[analysis] Pilot refinement for expert preference and multilingual data: retain an unfiltered calibration sample alongside the accepted sample. Score raw agreement, exclusions, adjudication and acceptance separately; inspect whether difficult but relevant cases disappear. HelpSteer2’s κ change is conditional on multistage filtering, Aya’s language total does not guarantee uniform contributor diversity or safety review, and Inherent Disagreements warns against pooling batch-normalized scales. Predeclare whether the buyer needs consensus labels, calibrated scalar attributes or a distribution of valid preferences before requesting a price per example.

## 11. Research outlook: testable judgments and open questions

[analysis] Hypothesis — stage-level provenance will become a more useful comparison than a binary human/synthetic label. The sample already contains human-authored preferences, model-generated feedback, synthetic educational scores and human correction of model responses. Confidence is moderate for the usefulness of this distinction and unestablished for its effect on procurement outcomes. The hypothesis would strengthen if provenance-complete manifests predict fewer acceptance surprises on matched tasks; it would weaken if those details fail to add information beyond ordinary samples and contracts. This is a research proposition, not a forecast of market adoption.

[analysis] Hypothesis — environment and verifier maintenance will be a distinct recurring delivery burden. Refresh describes versioned verifiers, OSWorld announces a verified-version change, and SWE-bench Multimodal reports repeated-test filtering. Confidence is moderate that version and stability matter within these examples, but the corpus supplies no market-wide maintenance cost. A longitudinal study should record environment breakage, verifier corrections and acceptance changes under frozen agents. If stable tasks require little upkeep across relevant software changes, the hypothesized burden would be narrower than suggested.

[analysis] Hypothesis — multilingual validity will require native task design as well as translation quality. M-IFEval modifies constraints, MENLO isolates local dimensions and BenchMAX post-edits translated data. Confidence is moderate for the methodological distinction, without an estimated commercial premium. A useful experiment would match translated, post-edited and native-authored tasks on intended constructs and independently score local failures. Equal validity under those controlled conditions would weaken the need for a separate native-authoring stage in that particular use case.

[analysis] Hypothesis — reliability reporting will need both repeated execution and disagreement preservation. τ-bench distinguishes all-trials reliability from at-least-one success, while DICES and the disagreement study expose meaningful variation in human labels. Confidence is high that these are different denominators; the effect on supplier selection remains untested. A matched pilot should compare decisions made from aggregate success alone with decisions using repeated trials, raw labels and adjudication reasons. The hypothesis would weaken if added detail does not change acceptance or predict deployment errors.

[analysis] Hypothesis — reward-model and monitor evaluations will need adversarial separation from the optimization loop. Summarization overoptimization, verifier search exploitation and the reasoning-monitor study demonstrate specific mechanisms by which optimization can outpace a proxy. Confidence is moderate for the need to test this risk, not for its prevalence in current services. Hold out failure classes and reviewer inputs when optimizing the system, then measure independent outcome errors. A robust matched study showing stable external validity across optimization intensity would narrow this concern.

CrowdWorkSheets asks for maintenance and pool-selection rationale; Datasheets asks about collection participants and compensation; the labor study warns about unknown population boundaries. Confidence is moderate for the research value of these fields, with no causal claim that publishing them improves wages or model quality. Follow-up research should compare documentation with consented worker evidence and project logs, retaining discrepancies and avoiding a disclosure-completeness score that masquerades as performance.

[research_gap] Priority evidence gaps: comparable accepted-unit economics; contributor-level paid-active windows; independent project outcomes; version-specific rights clearance; non-English and non-text coverage intersections; benchmark side-effect detection; and a complete source-supported supplier contribution map. The current graph’s richer catalogue does not resolve these automatically. Research should prioritize decision-changing evidence rather than optimize counts, and should document negative findings and unresolved cases alongside additions.

[method] The weekly outlook should be revised through falsifiable change conditions. Each stable executive finding records confidence, reasoning, limitations and what would change the assessment. New primary evidence can strengthen, narrow or supersede a finding; a changed source version should not silently overwrite its predecessor. A meaningful revision will identify which observed assumption changed and whether the effect is task-specific or supports a broader conclusion. No growth, revenue, employment or technology-adoption forecast is produced from this selected corpus.

[analysis] Hypothesis — a stronger documentation audit will improve diligence only if reporting signals are checked against project evidence. GIGO and Who Annotates observe disclosure, not undisclosed practice; the latter also exposes extraction uncertainty. Confidence is moderate in the need to distinguish those objects and unmeasured in the commercial value of an audit score. A follow-up could compare disclosed instructions, training and compensation fields with consented project records and independently sampled outputs. If completeness fails to predict agreement between disclosure and practice, its role should remain a transparency measure rather than a performance proxy.

## 12. Methods, coverage, bibliography and reproducible appendices

[method] Evidence boundary and source hierarchy. The factual boundary is the approved, validated merged graph selected by the explicit partition index. Discovery candidates, provisional reviews, search snippets and unpinned working files do not become report facts. Primary creator papers, official repository/card versions, provider policies, audited statements and first-party case accounts retain their source type. Provider marketing is reported as a disclosure. A source-content review checks whether an exact claim is supported; it does not transform self-reported operations into an independent audit.

[method] Assertion approval and review identity. Each approved assertion has exact-content author, source-verifier and adversarial receipts from separate actual AI invocations. Approval binds wording, subject, predicate, object or typed value, qualifications, source version, locator and excerpt digest. Report-level evidence-auditor and adversarial reviews are separate requirements bound to the exact report digest and complete graph digest. Prior report or graph reviews cannot approve this expanded synthesis. No fabricated human reviewer, honorific, institutional endorsement or review receipt is added.

[method] Original-stage notes and current status. Frozen source records retain historical author-only or proposal-stage wording where it was part of the original packet. Those notes describe that earlier stage and do not replace current status. This report reads approval from exact-digest three-role receipts while retaining source-depth and substantive limitations. Twenty-six later-disputed bindings remain candidate/history records; approved replacements use new IDs after fresh independent review. The original scientific values and qualifications are unchanged, and earlier positive or negative receipts and actual capture/review dates are not erased.

[method] Reading depth. full_source is a bounded editorial category: methods plus main results or worked examples and limitations, with separately recorded spans. It does not mean all appendices or proofs were read, every experiment reproduced or all corpus records checked. A truthful full_document_read false is compatible with adequate bounded main-section review. Abstract-only material cannot be promoted through a claim count. Dataset construction may be reviewed through creator methods and documentation without adding the original paper work as a fully reviewed paper or establishing corpus-byte identity.

[method] Capture-specific evidence. Cogito and Mindy observations bind the exact saved official extracted-page snapshots available to the reviewers; origin HTML and live HTTP status were not exposed by that extraction. Separate direct retrieval attempts had their own failures and do not turn the extraction into a verified live-origin response. The Mindy FAQ is undated, so current staffing/location figures are not adopted. TrustScale’s rebrand article was decoded from the pinned public application bundle rather than established by rendered-page execution. These capture boundaries remain attached to the underlying source records and dossier limitations.

[method] Version and identity accounting. A paper work counts once through its reviewed manifestation; a dataset or benchmark family counts once through approved family/release evidence. Formats, configs, splits and subset releases do not add families. FineWeb-Edu is currently one FineWeb subset release, correcting the initial eight-family baseline’s separate-family treatment without changing that archive’s bytes. MuSiQue’s new human-composed questions support one family; inherited seed corpora and answerability/serialization variants do not add families. Corporate aliases and product brands do not automatically add suppliers.

[method] Reproduction snapshot. This refreshed synthesis binds the validated merged graph with canonical JSON SHA-256 044a17dc52ae6e70d684e18fbf9dc6273be657aa6b80c1074a963f33513160d8. Canonical dataset version 2.5.0 and its exact-file SHA-256 948e69229fa24a4a1e6b5eed6d9c11570568a3c05bf9512e442d19611061a061 remain unchanged. Recompute the graph digest with research_report.canonical_hash after research_graph.load_graph validates indexed partitions and canonical bytes. This is a pinned synthesis input, not a frozen eligible-core inventory or a published archive. Any later graph change requires a new synthesis binding and actual separate report reviews.

[method] Computed coverage appendix. Coverage method 1.3.0 counts 1,713 approved assertions, 26 quarantined candidate assertions and 39 historical assertions. There are 1,790 scoped source records, of which 1,789 are captured; those captured records represent 503 distinct document versions under the version/response-hash rule. Multiple excerpts or locators can refer to one version and are not independent documents. The selected qualifying corpus contains 65 suppliers, 152 distinct paper works, 63 dataset families and 21 benchmark families. All 39 legacy organizations have completed bounded inclusion audits; 38 have conclusive commercial dispositions and BenchFlow remains commercially pending. These are separate measures, and no pending qualification contributes a qualifying supplier or frozen-core disposition.

[method] Relationship appendix. Exactly 216 approved assertions in this input use explicit object relationships. Other observations use source-bound typed values. Every predicate is nontransitive: parent links support work/family accounting only. A paper mentioning a company, using its software or documenting expert recruitment does not authorize an unstated supplier edge, exclusive authorship, contract value or causal performance attribution. Paper versions, dataset releases, formats, aliases and mirrors remain identity evidence rather than automatically creating additional counted objects.

[method] Launch gate appendix. The fixed floors require 39 completed legacy inclusion audits, 60 qualifying suppliers, 150 reviewed paper works, 60 dataset families, 20 benchmark families and disposition of at least 90% of a frozen eligible core. Commercial dispositions are separately reported; BenchFlow’s pending status does not invalidate its completed inclusion audit. The eligible core remains unfrozen. The formal reference and screening audits each require completed non-fixture holdouts and their source-bound, independently adjudicated provenance. Reference precision must reach 98% and recall 95% with no critical false attribution; screening needs at least 190 of 200 eligible records and at least 90% recall in each major stratum. Meeting numerical thresholds in a separate diagnostic does not complete these audits.

[method] Audit status and limitations. Formal reference and screening launch audits are incomplete; no approval count, schema pass or diagnostic threshold comparison changes that state. The eligible inventory remains a lower bound under active independent boundary-policy review. Open discovery partitions, unresolved identities and mandatory deep-review gaps prevent a final denominator, census claim or core disposition rate. Accessible and well-documented sources can remain overrepresented despite a large approved corpus. A pinned authoring graph and a frozen diagnostic sample are distinct from a completed, frozen eligible inventory.

[method] Search and selection bias. This is a selected public-source corpus rather than a probability sample. English-language material, public research artifacts and providers with detailed documentation are easier to discover and inspect. Confidential contracts, unavailable or blocked documents, undocumented suppliers and unobserved language/domain intersections can be missing. Unknown fields are preserved as unknown and do not count as evidence of absence. The report’s comparisons are sample-limited and should not be extrapolated into the entire market.

[method] Source dates and weekly cutoff. published_on records a document’s publication date when established; the event described may be older; captured_on records retrieval; reviewed_on records actual review; assertion as_of records its declared observation date; an edition needs an actual publication confirmation. The planned 13 November 17:00 Pacific cutoff and 16 November weekly check remain future schedule points in this 10 November prelaunch preparation. A later capture cannot be moved into an earlier window, and a delayed run is catch-up rather than a backdated publication.

[method] Interpretation and reproducible calculations. Approved counts are computed from qualifying identities and current approved assertions. Sample ratios should identify numerator and denominator before rounding. Project cost and acceptance formulas in chapter 8 are proposed methods with no invented inputs. Paper-reported results in the atlas retain the exact task, version and measurement condition described by the approved statement; they are not independently reproduced results, current model rankings or estimates of supplier performance. No metric is averaged across incompatible benchmark protocols.

[method] Public reuse and downloads. The research hub is https://sciencetostartup.com/research/; the living report route is https://sciencetostartup.com/research/state-of-ai-data-labs/; the evidence and download index is https://sciencetostartup.com/research/data/; source-backed review and correction entry is https://sciencetostartup.com/review/. Download links in the prepared publication must bind its own JSON/CSV/SQLite, schemas, bibliography, checksum manifest, offline evidence appendix, PDF and reproduction package. This source report does not assert that the expanded matching package, DOI, Zenodo archive or Hugging Face mirror already exists.

[method] Publication and corrections. Website preparation, deployment, archive confirmation and mirror synchronization have separate states and receipts. Accounts remain prepare-only under the current policy. A source-backed correction should identify the claim or report block, the source version and locator, the proposed wording and the reason. The research workflow reviews support, privacy and identity before integrating changes. Historical frozen packages retain pinned bytes; a correction belongs in a new version and change log rather than an invisible replacement.

[method] Bibliography reading guide. The entries below provide the reviewed paper-work title, a source URL from its bound evidence and the inspected source version. Claim links carry the exact locator, excerpt hash, qualifications and review identities. A source URL can resolve to a later page; the recorded version and response digest define the reviewed content. Dataset and supplier bibliography records are available through each atlas/dossier’s claim bindings and the evidence ledger; no external affiliation is used as a substitute for a documented contribution.

[method] Reference diagnostic, not launch audit. A private constructed challenge retains all 250 frozen cases sampled from the previously approved corpus. Two independent AI truth workers using the same requested model family established judgments with a third tie-breaker before comparison with the system under test; locator-context boundaries were clarified during adjudication. Under the strict consensus key, the unchanged run records 184 true positives, three false positives, two false negatives and 61 true negatives: precision 184/187 = 98.3957% and recall 184/186 = 98.9247%. These are challenge-specific results, not production accuracy, discovery recall, human peer review or completed reference-audit evidence.

[method] Diagnostic run binding and repair separation. The private reference-holdout-v1/diagnostic-results.v1.json run receipt has file SHA-256 870e45072181561da4203d256f97803b26a9ac0376573cb2024bd57d47b5f46e. Its consensus freeze is 1d6b81a6bf1cf80cc326ced6a3671ea0b100078d48d876360f6e8a63efddba3a and its evaluated-predictions digest is 7fe7d94ff17aa1f60c9339b72b85c33cea9a3df7baef0589cfa36a0b8ececb5c. Source-binding repairs are subsequent remediation. They do not remove or relabel challenge cases, replace the recorded predictions or revise the frozen diagnostic scores. Threshold comparisons leave unresolved formal audit provenance and protocol conditions held.

[method] Source-binding correction ledger. The 26 old-to-new mappings are preserved in the authoring correction ledger with file SHA-256 0ce874b0aacd4fbe9bd70a5074e28b8da0fdb8077bfbac65484344de70cd131c, bound to this exact graph. The ledger records newly approved replacement IDs and their 78 fresh three-role review IDs. This report remaps citations to those approved IDs while retaining the underlying scientific text and substantive qualifications. Original candidate IDs and earlier positive/negative review history remain available in the graph; fresh source review does not serve as an exact-report synthesis review.

[method] Locator reproduction. A locator identifies pinned source bytes and an extraction convention. One-based physical PDF pages differ from printed labels; global marked-text lines count markers and blank lines, while per-page pdftotext-layout coordinates use their declared physical page and tool convention. Preserve source versions, raw-response hashes and supplied derived-text hashes before interpreting a line range. Dataset-card revisions document the inspected card and do not automatically identify every corpus shard. A successful re-extraction is reproducibility evidence, rather than a new capture, scientific finding or independent content review.

## Evidence and reproduction

The accompanying clean-dataset.json, CSV and SQLite contain the same versioned public projection. Canonical dataset 2.5.0 remains unchanged outside this archive. Contact details and raw source text are excluded from this projection. Review receipts describe actual scope. corrections.json records accepted correction metadata and approved replacements; evidence.html preserves superseded IDs without unapproved wording. Candidate assertions and metadata-only discoveries are excluded from approved evidence; completed inclusion audits may leave commercial qualification unresolved.

Open evidence.html for offline entity dossiers, a recorded-scope comparison table, assertions, source bindings and review receipts. Use MANIFEST.json to verify each file's SHA-256. The archive is self-contained and makes no network requests. Source URLs and identifiers are retained in the accompanying public graph.
